description: The FROM phrase of WRITE, REWRITE and RELEASE with a literal operand (a figurative constant included) - a COBOL-2002 introduction. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): ANSI X3.23-1985 prints `WRITE record-name-1 [ FROM identifier-1 ]` (§1985:VII.4.7.2), `REWRITE record-name-1 [ FROM identifier-1 ] [ END-REWRITE ]` (§1985:VII.4.5.2) and `RELEASE record-name-1 [ FROM identifier-1 ]` (§1985:XI.4.2.2), an identifier only; ISO/IEC 1989:2002 prints `FROM { identifier-1 | literal-1 }` in all three (§2002:14.8.47.1, §2002:14.8.33.1, §2002:14.8.30.1), with §2002:14.8.47.2 SR6 'If record-name-1 is specified, identifier-1 or literal-1 shall be valid as a sending operand in a MOVE statement specifying record-name-1 as the receiving operand' (§2002:14.8.33.2 SR6 the same; §2002:14.8.30.2 SR3 'Identifier-1 or literal-1 shall be valid as a sending operand in a MOVE statement specifying record-name-1 as the receiving operand'), and §2002:F.2 states the change, its item 148: 'A record can be written from a literal using the WRITE, RELEASE, or REWRITE statement.' §2014:14.9.47.2 SR6 and §2014:14.9.30.2 SR3 carry the 2002 rules unchanged, so 2014 = 2023 (§2023:14.9.51.3 SR6, §2023:14.9.35.3 SR6, §2023:14.9.32.3 SR3; VCR row 7.34). ONE grammar rule (recordFromPhrase) carries the phrase for all three statements and ONE parse-arm gate (VisitRecordFromPhrase) asks its edge (kb/Work PB2650: the gate used to be RELEASE's alone).

IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. RWRFL.
ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
FILE-CONTROL.
    SELECT F ASSIGN TO "rwrfl.dat"
        ORGANIZATION IS SEQUENTIAL.
    SELECT S-F ASSIGN TO "rwrfl.tmp".
DATA DIVISION.
FILE SECTION.
FD F.
01 F-REC PIC X(5).
SD S-F.
01 S-REC PIC X(5).
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 W-REC PIC X(5).
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    OPEN OUTPUT F.
    WRITE F-REC FROM "HELLO".
    CLOSE F.
    OPEN I-O F.
    READ F.
    REWRITE F-REC FROM SPACE.
    CLOSE F.
    SORT S-F ON ASCENDING KEY S-REC
        INPUT PROCEDURE IS IP
        OUTPUT PROCEDURE IS OP.
    STOP RUN.
IP.
    RELEASE S-REC FROM "HELLO".
OP.
    RETURN S-F INTO W-REC AT END CONTINUE END-RETURN.
